title: Ultra Heaven
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a near future where mind-altering drugs are legal and served in 'pump bars' by medically licensed bartenders, the addict Kabu (Cub in the English edition) chases ever stronger highs, including near-death experiences. A mysterious pusher gives him a new hallucinogen he names 'Ultra Heaven', and the line between trip and reality collapses into nightmare, overdose and visions of paradise, while shadowy figures seem to be experimenting on him. The psychedelic, unfinished series asks what is real (Wikipedia; Last Gasp blurb; TCJ review).
life_message: A life spent chasing the ultimate high dissolves the self and leaves nothing real to stand on.

content.note: In a nightmare trip Kabu kills two sanitation officers and is shot in the head; grotesque body imagery (Wikipedia; TCJ review).
Nightmarish hallucinations, body dissolving into objects, brain-death scare (Wikipedia; TCJ review; MU Hallucination/s, Mind Break).
AniList Nudity tag at low rank; no sexual content in summaries or review (to verify).

Drug use is the core subject: dangerous mixtures, addiction, relapse, overdose; reviewer calls it critical but not moralizing, with highs drawn as exhilarating (Wikipedia; TCJ review; AniList Drugs; MU Drug Abuse/Addiction).
Kabu has suicidal tendencies and seeks near-death highs; people attempt suicide by mixing drugs (Wikipedia; TCJ review).
Detailed drug-mixing and dosing culture; relapse after trying to quit (Wikipedia).
Drugs freely advertised on TV in the setting (MU description).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Society legalizes drugs and leaves people to choose, with hygiene offices policing a few.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Shadowy authorities experiment on Kabu, but rank is not celebrated.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Pharmaceutical, technocratic world; transcendence sought chemically.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Pursuit of subjective experience over security.

folkways.japan: Japan's very strict drug laws make the premise of fully legal 'pump bars' a pointed dystopian inversion.

delivery.evidence: TCJ reviewer calls it critical but not moralizing, reflective rather than preachy.

personified.ideology: the dream is more real than life

delivery.note: The work makes the highs feel exhilarating while showing their cost, leaving readers to draw conclusions.

winners_losers: No one wins: Kabu's pursuit of the ultimate high leaves him lost between dream and reality, while the pusher and hidden experimenters hold power.
